solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Medicine man in large consignment from Africa?

definitions.meaning: the Greek physician regarded as the father of medicine
read whimsically, boxes of river horses shipped out of Africa: HIPPO plus CRATES

explanation.surface: Asks whether a doctor is hiding among a big shipment from Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is playful: split the name as HIPPO CRATES, packing cases of large African animals.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek physician of the oath is the archetypal doctor, so he is literally a man of medicine.

definitions.meaning: something thrilling or sexy, in slang
literally material at a very high temperature, lava being one example

explanation.surface: Describes something thrilling by comparing it to molten lava.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang phrase means anything or anyone very exciting or attractive, and taken literally it fits glowing lava.

clue.text: Prenatal and paternal problems of mum and dad?

indicators.note: the letters of the word are in trouble, so they are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Suggests the troubles a mother and father face before and after a birth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problems' signals the anagram; 'and paternal' is a second word with the same letters, adding to the surface without being needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something relating to a mother and father, as in care given by the household's mother and father.

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters spanning the words limbo and uncertain

explanation.surface: A cat is stuck in limbo, unsure of what comes next.
explanation.definitionFit: The snow leopard, a big wild cat, is also called by this name.

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
tile is old slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A salesman in a hat is written off as a nasty piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: TILE for a hat is dated British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A contemptible, cold-blooded person is figuratively called a snake or lizard-like creature.

parts.note: the phrase bare-chested appears with its first letter, its top, removed, so it is itself without a top

explanation.walkthrough: The clue shows 'bare-chested' missing its first letter: it has lost its top, and someone bare-chested is also without a top.
explanation.definitionFit: Going without a shirt or upper garment leaves the upper body uncovered, i.e. bare to the waist.

clue.text: Perform top parts, for crying out loud!

indicators.note: parts means splits open, so the word for perform is separated to hold the other piece

parts.note: to perform a song is to sing
the cream is the top, the best part, rising to the surface of milk

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry at someone who performs only the top parts of a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' reads as roles in a performance, but it is the verb: the singing is parted to take the top in.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrieking or yelling describes someone making a loud piercing noise.

clue.text: Where flu may have come from scrubbing in bath

indicators.note: scrubbing means cancelling, so the letters of in are struck out

parts.words: Where flu may have come from
parts.note: the 1918 pandemic was called Spanish flu, pointing to Spain

explanation.surface: Wonders whether a bout of flu was caught at the baths.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'scrubbing in bath' as washing; it is the deletion signal, and Bath, a city with Roman baths, is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bath in the English west country is a famous spa town, so it is an example of one.

clue.text: Jack, boy dressing in the morning

indicators.note: a dressing is stuffing, so these letters are packed into the name

parts.note: Sean is a boy's name
a.m. is the abbreviation for morning hours

explanation.surface: A boy named Jack is getting dressed in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack, or jack tar, is an old nickname for a sailor.

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of
a king is a royal

explanation.surface: Someone striking a pose like a member of the royal family.
explanation.definitionFit: Posing a question is putting it, i.e. enquiring.

indicators.note: back tells us the word for track is read from right to left

parts.note: a rut is a track worn in the ground
someone visiting is in

explanation.surface: Following a route back on a visit to a city in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Piedmont capital in northern Italy is a major city on the continent.

parts.note: FT, the Financial Times, is the paper; FT written back to front gives the clue's letters

explanation.surface: A bare abbreviation asking what kind of book it might be.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer read as instructions, a paper (FT) back, produces TF.
explanation.definitionFit: A softcover volume is one kind of book.

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so these letters are broken up and remade

explanation.surface: Something from another clue going into a piece of ground.
explanation.walkthrough: '17' points to the answer of 17 down, a small citrus fruit; this answer is a variety of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A small loose-skinned orange citrus fruit is one variety of the fruit at 17.

parts.note: an Aga is a brand of kitchen range, a heavy cast-iron cooker
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A range of goods is popular once more.
explanation.walkthrough: AGA is a British brand of big cast-iron kitchen stove, a range.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: doing something another time is doing it a second time.

clue.text: Intended payment to secure him a snack, regularly

indicators.note: to secure is to hold fast, so the fee wraps round the other letters

parts.note: a fee is a payment

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the words him a snack

explanation.surface: A planned payment to get someone a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intended' looks like an adjective about the payment, but it is the noun for a future spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman engaged to be married is a man's intended, his bride-to-be.

clue.text: Most devious ref's tactic almost absurd

indicators.note: absurd means nonsensical, so the letters are thrown into a new order
almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

explanation.surface: A referee's tactic is judged absurd and most devious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims TACTIC to TACTI; 'absurd' rearranges REFS plus TACTI.
explanation.definitionFit: Being the most cunning and sly of all is being the most underhand or devious.

indicators.note: knocking a glass over turns it upside down, so the word for lager is read backwards
over completes the phrase about toppling the beer, reversing its letters

parts.note: Pils, short for Pilsner, is a type of lager

explanation.surface: An accident of tipping over a glass of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A small error or blunder, as in a slip of the tongue.

definitions.meaning: slang for a prison sentence, time inside
a hot oat dish eaten in the morning

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stir' looks like a cooking instruction for the breakfast but is British slang for a stretch in prison, as is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is British slang for time served in jail and also the oatmeal dish eaten in the morning.

definitions.meaning: a powerful senior official, originally of imperial China

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a senior bureaucrat with clout and a small loose-skinned orange fruit.

definitions.meaning: middling, as in a performance that was only so-so

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'Pretty' as an adverb meaning quite; it is an adjective, one of two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word can mean attractive in old usage and also merely average or moderate.

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
a page is a young servant

explanation.surface: An accusation against a male servant, or an order to attack.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge about wildly is to run riot, smashing things.

clue.text: Venetian lady soaring all over the place

indicators.note: all over the place means scattered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lady of Venice soars about in every direction.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian title for a married woman, the counterpart of Mrs, fits a woman from Venice.

indicators.note: taking means holding, so the ship's letters hold the word for private

parts.note: on board conventionally means inside SS, the steamship abbreviation
inner means private, as in one's inner thoughts

explanation.surface: Wrongdoers taking a soldier on board a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'private' looks like a soldier but is an adjective; 'on board' supplies the SS round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who transgress against moral or religious law are offenders.

parts.note: wit is clever humour
a hit is a success

explanation.surface: A joke told with clever humour lands as a success.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fashionable or up to date with trends is being in, i.e. hip.

definitions.meaning: a famous English public school in north-west London

explanation.walkthrough: The school is an old fee-paying boarding school in London; the verb means to distress.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of an English public school is also a verb for causing great distress.

clue.text: Unbecoming taking forty winks during technology lessons

indicators.note: during means within the time of, so the sleep sits inside the lessons

parts.note: IT is information technology, a school subject
forty winks is a short sleep, a nap

explanation.surface: A pupil dozing off in a computing class is behaving badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsuitable or inappropriate behaviour is unbecoming.

clue.text: With lovely hands, my better male patient?

parts.note: the patient here is a man
read as 'I cured', my making someone better

explanation.surface: A doctor boasts about a male patient's fine hands after treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer split as MAN I CURED: the man is the patient and 'my better' says I made him better.
explanation.definitionFit: Hands that have been professionally trimmed and polished look attractive and well-groomed.

clue.text: Moderate shock perhaps after first of calamities

indicators.note: after places the shock word behind the initial letter
first of means just the initial letter of calamities is taken

parts.note: a shock is a thick mass of hair

explanation.surface: Mild shock after the first of several disasters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' suggests surprise, but here a shock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: To chair a meeting is to preside over it, keeping debate in order.

clue.text: Loveless beauty cuddled by old poet in Derby, perhaps?

indicators.note: cuddled by means held inside the poet's name

parts.note: Horace was a Roman poet

indicators.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O, so loveless means that letter is removed

parts.note: a rose is a beauty

explanation.surface: A beauty spurned by love finds comfort with an old poet at Derby.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is zero in tennis scoring, hence O. The Derby is a famous English flat race for horses run at Epsom, not the city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Derby is an example of a contest between galloping thoroughbreds, a famous one.

parts.note: a venomous snake whose name also means one who sums up figures

explanation.walkthrough: 'Calculating' looks like scheming, but it is literal: one who adds up, also the name of Britain's venomous snake.
explanation.definitionFit: The viper is a venomous snake, and someone who totals numbers can be described with the same word.

indicators.note: initially means taking the first letter of each of the words the other way

explanation.surface: Pulling in the opposite direction, at first.
explanation.definitionFit: To haul a vehicle or boat along behind is to pull it.

parts.note: the plane is a tree, not an aircraft; the doctor is one who tends trees

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a medical emergency on a flight; the plane is a tree, so the doctor is an arborist.
explanation.definitionFit: An arborist who cuts and treats diseased trees, such as a London plane, is a doctor for timber.
